heading: News Today from Rajdeep Sardesai
paragraphs: President Donald Trump is set to sign the Russia sanctions bill after it cleared both chambers of Congress. The legislation allows him to impose tariffs of up to 100% on major buyers of Russian energy, including India and China. What could this mean for India-US ties and global energy markets? Could a prolonged court battle damage the Tata brand, irrespective of who wins? Is a compromise necessary? With Tata Sons reappointing N Chandrasekaran despite Noel Tata's objections, will the decision stand? And after more than five decades across cinema, theatre and television, Anant Nag has been chosen for the Dadasaheb Phalke Award. Was the honour long overdue? Does theatre remain his first love, or has cinema taken its place? The veteran actor speaks exclusively to India Today. Three major conversations, tonight on News Today with Rajdeep Sardesai.

This special News Today broadcast covers key economic, geopolitical, and national developments. The programme examines the political and economic debate surrounding the levy of a 0.4 percent merchant discount rate on Unified Payments Interface transactions exceeding 2,000 rupees.
This special broadcast covers key civic, economic, and public safety developments across India.

The programme examines the growing global debate over AI safety after Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned, warning of existential risks from unchecked development, and looks at Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's three-step framework for AI safeguards and international coordination.
Chinese President Xi Jinping is set to visit New Delhi on Saturday for the 18th BRICS Summit, marking his first India visit in seven years.

Chinese President Xi Jinping visits New Delhi on September 12 to participate in the BRICS Summit, marking his first trip to India in seven years. The multilateral gathering features key bilateral engagements involving Prime Minister Narendra Modi, President Xi, and Russian President Vladimir Putin, focusing on India-China border negotiations, trade relations, economic cooperation, and global diplomacy. Alongside summit coverage, this special report examines registered unrecognized political parties across Gujarat, Delhi, Bihar, and Madhya Pradesh that collected substantial donations while operating from residential sites and locked offices without contesting elections. Former Chief Election Commissioner Dr S.Y. Quraishi and transparency activist Anjali Bhardwaj analyze statutory income tax exemptions, regulatory loopholes, and Election Commission oversight, while also addressing widespread voter list deletions flagged during the Special Intensive Revision in Delhi and Karnataka.

Municipal authorities in Delhi initiated demolition drives against unsafe buildings and imposed regulatory curbs on paying guest accommodations after a building collapse in Satya Niketan resulted in seven fatalities.
This News Today primetime special report examines major news developments across India and internationally.

A multi-storey paying guest accommodation collapsed in Delhi's Satya Niketan, resulting in seven fatalities, including five Delhi University students, and injuring five others. The Delhi Chief Minister suspended five Municipal Corporation of Delhi officials, including a deputy commissioner, while police arrested the building owner, Hariram Gupta, alongside his wife and son. The Delhi High Court ordered a high-level probe and directed municipal authorities to inspect all paying guest facilities within a week. Additionally, structural audits were mandated across student hubs such as Mukherjee Nagar, Rajendra Nagar, and Saket. A panel discussion featuring former Urban Development Secretary Dr. Sudhir Krishna addressed systemic municipal corruption, structural violations, and unauthorized constructions in Delhi and Gurugram. The segment also covers an India Today ground report detailing a severe teacher shortage in Himachal Pradesh government schools, where assembly data reveals 150 schools operate without any teachers and over 3,500 rely on a single teacher, prompting recruitment assurances from Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu.
A national debate has emerged over India's first-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) growth figures of 7.8 percent, following criticisms raised by former Finance Secretary Subhash Chandra Garg.
The Indian government's announcement of a 7.8% GDP growth rate for the first quarter has triggered political debate and economic analysis.
In an interview with Rajdeep Sardesai, Lobsang Sangay, former Prime Minister of the Tibetan government-in-exile, raised serious concerns over the impact of recent Himalayan flash floods in Tibet.

The Indian economy grew 7.8% in the April-June quarter, beating expectations despite oil price shocks from the Iran war. Meanwhile, two Indian-born women adopted by different families in the Netherlands discovered nearly four decades later that they are biological sisters. Mina Gelting and Minal Taijon, friends since meeting at a camp in 1996, learnt the truth through a DNA test and now plan to travel together to Mumbai to trace their roots. Watch NewsToday With Rajdeep Sardesai.
This News Today episode sheds light on the growing public scrutiny of the Indian economy, a key theme in the Mood of the Nation poll.

A catastrophic flash flood triggered by a massive ice and rock avalanche in the high Himalayan region has caused widespread devastation across Nepal, leaving over 350 people dead and hundreds missing near the Nepal-China border.

A massive flash flood in Nepal has killed at least 95 people and left more than 400 foreign nationals missing, including 133 Indian tourists, after the disaster struck the Kerung border customs office near the Nepal-China border. The key route used by Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims was swept by raging floodwaters, with 77 Indian pilgrims associated with the Isha Foundation among those reportedly missing. More than 50 of the missing Indian tourists are from Tamil Nadu. The floods also swept away the Langtang Khola hydropower project in Rasuwa district, leaving around 60 employees missing, besides destroying motorable bridges and inundating parts of the Trishuli region. Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke to Nepalese Prime Minister Balen Shah, conveyed condolences and offered India's full humanitarian assistance. An IAF C-130J Super Hercules aircraft carrying 10 tonnes of relief material has been sent to Kathmandu, while a C-17 Globemaster remains on standby. Rescue operations are being hampered by difficult terrain, mud, sludge and adverse weather.

Rishikesh Kumar, an MSc Physics student at IIT Delhi, died after jumping from the sixth floor of the Lecture Hall Complex. Police said no suicide note was found and are examining his counselling records, mobile phone and other material. The death has again raised questions over why IITs continue to struggle to prevent student suicides despite counselling systems and mental-health interventions on campuses. In another major development, recurring waterlogging has put Gurugram's urban planning under scrutiny, raising questions over why the Millennium City floods year after year. Environmentalist Vaishali Rana said most of Gurugram's 550 km stormwater drain network is encroached upon, including 18 km of the 28-km Badshapur Nala. Retired engineer Dr Shiv Singh Rawat blamed excessive concretisation and years of poor planning for reducing the city's ability to absorb rainwater. Architect Dikshu Kukreja said master plans have failed to account for Gurugram's natural topography and called for blue-green infrastructure, permeable surfaces and climate-focused planning. The discussion also focused on administrative accountability and better town planning to tackle the city's recurring flooding.

In an exclusive interview, agricultural economist Professor Ashok Gulati explained the factors behind the sharp rise in sugar prices ahead of India's festive season, pointing to lower production, declining opening stocks and the diversion of sugarcane towards ethanol blending. He criticised the government's delayed response, saying, "Government has miscalculated the shortage," and argued that measures such as reducing import duties should have been taken six to eight months earlier. Gulati also called for greater market-oriented liberalisation, futures trading and reduced political intervention in the sugar sector. The episode also touches upon key national and international developments, including Maharashtra's FDA suspending licences of nine Mumbai eateries over hygiene violations, a row over Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy's US visit, and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay putting the proposed Parandur airport project on hold. Internationally, 21 former cricket captains, including Sunil Gavaskar and Kapil Dev, sought medical care for jailed former Pakistan PM Imran Khan.

In this India Today video, anchor Preeti Chaudhury reports on Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi's six-hour dharna outside the Sansad Marg Police Station in Delhi, following allegations of pellet gun injuries sustained by student Sahil Lochab during a paper leak protest. The protest ended after Delhi Police registered an FIR in the case.
